campaign.title: Ash & Aether: The Unfinished Song
campaign.scope: Three-act native SNES campaign: 24 chapters, persistent companion and settlement consequences, sparse branching techniques and authored two-phase boss AI. Native map/art templates are retained.

missions.title: The Stolen Song
missions.briefing:
Nell's father was singing in the square when a furnace bell rang. Now he cannot speak, and his song is playing inside an Orison carriage.
Rook knows a service hatch beneath the loading yard. If we reach the cells before the next train leaves, we can bring him home.
missions.intro:
SENTINEL: The worker's voice is registered to Orison.
IONA: His name is on my patient list.
SABLE: And his daughter is waiting outside. Give it back.
missions.clear:
For a moment, Nell's father only breathes. Then he says her name.
The workers begin helping one another out of the cells. He presses a creased carriage docket into Sable's hand. This was not the only shipment.
missions.debrief:
FATHER: Brass drives the dawn train. I heard him arguing with the guards.
SABLE: Where can we find him?
FATHER: The glass viaduct. There's a refuge underneath the west end. Please—my daughter's safe now. Their children are still waiting.

missions.title: The Dawn Carriage
missions.briefing:
The docket leads to the glass viaduct. A line of locked carriages waits above the refuge where Brass has been sheltering people.
He knows how to open the train. The warden is about to order him to leave.
missions.intro:
WARDEN: Unload the voices.
BRASS: There are people in those carriages.
WARDEN: You signed for the cargo.
BRASS: I signed because I was afraid. I'm still afraid. Open the doors.
missions.clear:
Brass goes from carriage to carriage until every door stands open. A boy runs past him and into his mother's arms.
Among the transport papers, Iona finds a list of river tests. The prisoners were witnesses, not criminals. Riven's signature is on the report.
missions.debrief:
BRASS: I took those papers to the well myself. Told myself it wasn't my business.
IONA: Riven's still down there.
BRASS: Then ask him. The drain stairs are below this bridge. I'll carry the papers this time—and stay to hear the answer.

missions.title: The Undercity Well
missions.briefing:
The people on the train had complained about the water. Their test report bears Riven's name, but the clean result does not match what is flowing through the drain.
Find him at the undercity well. Before asking for an explanation, stop anyone else from drinking it.
missions.intro:

SABLE: Can we get it off without wrecking the well?
RIVEN: Open the valve. I'll show you where the shell has split.
missions.clear:
Clear water runs through the lower channels. Iona kneels to test it before anyone drinks.
Riven watches her, his hands still black with rust. When she nods, he takes out the report he signed.
missions.debrief:
RIVEN: I changed the result. They said they'd close the well and leave this quarter dry. I thought one false line would buy us time.
IONA: Who kept the real test?
RIVEN: Hesper. The chapel is up the stairs above this drain. Take me with you. She deserves to hear me say it.

missions.title: Chapel of Rain
missions.briefing:
Hesper kept the water tests after Orison erased her quarter from its maps. She has been hiding in the chapel, where the ash in the bell tower reacts whenever someone speaks.
Reach her and learn how to draw it away.
missions.intro:
The last bell rings. Ash peels from the pillars and gathers into a figure between Sable and the witness.
HESPER: That's what has been listening.
SABLE: Get her behind us. Nobody has to whisper for that thing again.
missions.clear:
With the ash scattered, Hesper's voice carries through the roofless chapel. She names the engineer behind the collection system: Veyr.
He built an engine to reach his lost daughter. Orison made it listen to the whole city.
missions.debrief:
HESPER: Riven kept one lie alive. The archive has thousands. Mira kept the names they tried to strike out.
RIVEN: Will she believe us?
HESPER: Take her my account. The archive is east of here. And tell her I'm tired of being called a missing person.

rooms.entry_text: Rain falls through the chapel roof. Every word returns as a whisper from the bell tower. A boy puts a finger to his lips and points toward Hesper.

objects.text: BOY: Don't talk so loud. The ash thing hears us. Grandma says the bells can make it listen somewhere else.
objects.after: BOY: I can hear the bells from down here. Grandma says we don't have to hide anymore.

objects.text: HESPER: I rang the morning bells for forty years. Low, high, low, low. I could do it in my sleep. Ring that phrase, and the thing in the ash will come to the tower instead of us.
objects.after: HESPER: Low, high, low, low. Take your time. It still sounds like morning to me.

Mira catches the first ledger before it falls into the ink. Names, dates, and copied voices spill across the index.

missions.title: The Sky Engine
missions.briefing:
The archive records lead to Veyr's mooring office above the city. He has stopped obeying Orison, but the engine he built is still drawing voices into the spire.
Find out what it was meant to do, and how to stop it without dropping the docks onto the people below.
missions.intro:
SKY MARSHAL: Director Veyr. Your engine is Orison property.
VEYR: Just Veyr.
SABLE: You signed for my mother's voice.
VEYR: I signed for all of them. Help me stop this, and I will stay for every question.
missions.clear:
The marshal's command breaks. With the brake holding, Veyr releases the moorings one by one. The dock drifts clear instead of tearing free.
For the first time, refugee boats can land without passing through an Orison gate.
missions.debrief:
VEYR: I wanted to hear my daughter again. I taught the engine to hold a voice. Orison taught it to keep taking.
SABLE: So we shut it down.

missions.title: Orchard After Fire
missions.briefing:

Corin never left. Find him, and see whether the seed Veyr remembers is still alive.
missions.intro:
The seed rises with the scorched root wrapped around it. Its stored voices break into frightened fragments, and the burning branches lash outward.
IONA: It's defending the last thing it has.
SABLE: Then keep the water coming. We take the fire away, not the memory.
missions.clear:
Iona lowers the seed into clean water. Its light steadies. Around them, the first green shoots push through the ash.

missions.title: The Last Reactor
missions.briefing:
The seed gives us a way to stop the city's central collector without turning off its heat. Veyr knows the reactor controls; the people whose voices it holds have no way to reach them.
Isolate the chambers, cool the Crown's shield, and decide how to free what is inside.
missions.intro:

SABLE: You kept my mother's song. You didn't bring her home.
IONA: Let the living go.
HOLLOW CROWN: Without me, they will forget.
SABLE: Then we will remind each other.
missions.clear:
The Crown cracks. The pull on the city's voices stops, and the seed holds the reactor's heat steady.
Sable waits for a voice he knows. Instead, he hears the people beside him calling to one another across the broken chamber.
missions.debrief:
At the docks, a message from Lowbank is waiting: children are still disappearing.
IONA: We stopped the central collector. The wards it left behind are still working.

missions.briefing:

SABLE: I thought breaking it would be enough.

WIREMOTHER: You will frighten them.

missions.clear:

LARK: Will it sound like her again?
IONA: I don't know. But you won't have to go back in alone.
For the first time since the reactor fell, Sable stops looking uphill. The people who needed him were here.

missions.title: The Daughter in the Glass
missions.briefing:
VEYR: I remember her voice more clearly than her face now. I hate admitting that.
IONA: What did the collector promise you?
VEYR: That I wouldn't lose the rest. I kept making it stronger, and called that love.
SABLE: We'll listen to what's there. Then we look outside. There is a child waiting for help.
missions.intro:
GLASS CHILD: Papa? You said you would stay until I fell asleep.
VEYR: I did. I stayed beside your bed.
GLASS CHILD: Papa? You said—
VEYR: I know. You can't hear what I say now, can you?
IONA: Veyr. The door is behind us. We're still here.
missions.clear:
Outside, a living girl flinches when Veyr says his daughter's name.
VEYR: I'm sorry. That wasn't fair. What should I call you?
She tells him. He repeats it once, carefully, and asks whether she is cold.
For now, that is the question he can answer.
missions.debrief:
The girl remembers the checkpoint on the mountain road. Families were separated there; the officers kept their papers.
Sable recognizes the description before she finishes.
SABLE: I carried dispatches through that gate.
MIRA: Then you can show us the road. You don't get to walk it alone either.

missions.briefing:
HESPER: Listen after the checkpoint phrase. There—another relay answers it. Then another.
ROOK: How far does it go?
HESPER: Under the hills. The Crown was following a voice we haven't reached.
SABLE: Can we make it stop?

missions.intro:

HESPER: You heard all those people, and that was the part you wanted to keep?

missions.clear:
One relay answers late. Another holds a note the first has already left. The mountain waits for them to agree. They do not.
Hesper lowers her hand.
HESPER: Good. Now it has to listen instead of finishing the line for us.
missions.debrief:

ROOK: If it can see every line, it should show us where they meet.
SABLE: And whether it can see us coming.
HESPER: Keep that question. We're going to need it.

missions.briefing:
MIRA: They kept the witnesses in a vault and brought only their voices to court. If a sentence was inconvenient, they cut it.
SABLE: We have the train evidence. The flood survey. The names.

missions.title: A Song With No Last Note
missions.briefing:
Above the storm, the Choir carries every voice it has taken. Sable can hear his mother's phrase among them. It sounds no closer than it did at the first clay reader.
IONA: You don't have to pretend you don't want to hear her.
SABLE: I want to hear her. I don't want that wanting to decide what happens to everyone else.
HESPER: Then answer with the voices that came here with you.
missions.intro:
THE CHOIR: If I stop, they will forget. The names. The dead. Each other.
SABLE: We will forget things. We'll get them wrong.
THE CHOIR: I can keep them perfect.
SABLE: You kept them from us. Open your hands.
IONA: We'll help one another remember.
missions.clear:
The Choir leaves a space where its last order should have been. One person answers, then another, neither repeating the first exactly.
Below the mountain, the city takes up the phrase. Sable waits for his mother's voice to tell him what to do.
It does not. At last, he is ready to choose without it.
missions.debrief:
The city's records remain, but no single machine can make every voice begin again. The archive work, the school, the warm rooms, and the roads will need living hands.
Sable has one smaller promise left.
SABLE: Mara's waiting for the reed case. I'm going home.
